# gh-798: [BUG] sm-silent-update pushes under an in-flight rework leg — timer auto-save push fails non-fast-forward mid-run (live: fa PR #1420, run 37828431528)

## Description

## Goal — Silent-update vs in-flight rework: the race that breaks the agent's timer pushes (v1)

One sentence: **a rework leg never again fights the SM's own silent branch refresh — `silent-update-behind` gains an in-flight-rework exclusion, and the harness-side timer push learns to survive a legitimate mid-run base refresh.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415 rework leg, run 37828431528, 2026-10-08):
- 19:13 — harness timer WIP auto-save pushed fine.
- 19:15:20 — `sm-silent-update` merged main into `ai/gh-1415` and pushed `f76db206` **while the rework leg was running on that branch**.
- 19:18 — second timer auto-save committed locally on the now-stale branch.
- 19:23 — timer push `git push origin HEAD` → **rejected (non-fast-forward), exit 1** — "⏱️ timer: git push failed" surfaced to the agent mid-run.
- 19:28 — the agent manually recovered (merged origin, pushed the real fix `d11a5670`, closed 4/4 review threads).

The leg survived by improvisation. The race is real: `silent-update-behind` excludes `ai_validating` ("so the validation head never moves mid-run") but has **no exclusion for an in-flight rework/review leg**, whose session is anchored to the exact branch state it checked out.

## Why this framing

- The rework leg's post-action, prompts, and thread-preparation (`preCliReworkSetup.js` → `pr_discussions.md`) all behaved correctly on this incident — the break was the mid-run base move, not the input pipeline.
- `ai_validating` exclusion already establishes the precedent: heads with a leg in flight must not move. This card extends the same invariant to rework/review legs.

## Architecture

1. **SM side (`js/smAgent.js` silent-update-behind / the shared `update_branch` path):** exclude PRs with an in-flight rework or review leg from silent refresh — the same detection the rerun/other rules already use (the `hasActiveHeadRun` pattern: any dispatched rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` run on the head in `queued`/`in_progress`, or the `agent:rework` label while a leg runs). The refresh is not lost — the PR is BEHIND and refreshes on the first tick after the leg finishes.
2. **Harness-side hardening (`pushReworkChanges.js` post-action and/or the timer push wrapper — whichever owns the bare `git push origin HEAD`):** a non-fast-forward rejection must self-heal — `git pull --no-rebase` (merge, matching the SM's own merge-style refreshes) then retry the push, once, before surfacing the failure. The agent's manual recovery (merge origin → push) is exactly this; encode it.
3. Ordering invariant: the exclusion must be checked at tick time (fresh state), not cached — an in-flight leg starts/stops between ticks.

## Capability surface

| path | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| rework/review leg in flight + PR BEHIND | silent-update pushes under the leg → timer push non-FF fails mid-run | leg excluded from refresh until it finishes; refresh happens on the next tick |
| timer push hits non-FF anyway (any residual race) | raw failure surfaced to the agent | one auto pull-merge + retry, then honest failure |
| validation legs | excluded (ai_validating) | unchanged |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — silent-update skips a BEHIND PR whose head has an in-flight (queued or running) rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` dispatch; refresh happens on the tick after the leg completes.
- **AC2** — the exclusion is evaluated per tick (a leg that finished between ticks does not block the refresh).
- **AC3** — a non-FF timer/post-action push self-heals via one pull-merge + retry and lands the commit (unit-tested push wrapper with a mock remote that rejects once).
- **AC4** — validation exclusion behavior unchanged (existing tests green).

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — silent-update query/action tests: mocked PR with in-flight dispatch (queued and running variants) → no push command emitted; leg finished → push emitted.
- `UT-*` — push-wrapper test: first push rejected non-FF → pull-merge → retry succeeds (AC3).
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green on the dmtools runtime; existing silent-update tests stay green (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Changing the validation-leg exclusion semantics.
- Making silent-update rebase instead of merge (the SM's merge-style refresh is load-bearing elsewhere).
- Harness-repo changes (the push wrapper lives in the rework job's JS / factory scripts, both in this repo's orbit).

## Open questions

- Whether the exclusion keys on the dispatch-run probe alone or also on the `agent:rework`/`agent:review` labels (recommend: the run probe — labels are set/cleared by the legs themselves and can be stale).

## References

- Live timeline: run 37828431528 (16:07 leg → 19:13/19:18 WIP saves, 19:15 silent-update `f76db206`, 19:23 push failure, 19:28 agent self-recovery `d11a5670`, 4/4 threads resolved).
- `silent-update-behind` rule (ai_validating exclusion rationale, limit 20); `preCliReworkSetup.js` (input prep, correct); `pushReworkChanges.js` (post-action push owner).

- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37835258454) · started 19:53 · done 20:05 ✅

**Fix** (mechanical):

The code fix itself is sound — this is only the missing docs regeneration, but it is a red merge gate and must land before merge.

### Thread 2 — `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the bare `'behind'` substring is a loose non-FF signal**

`isNonFastForwardError` treats *any* error text containing `behind` as a healable non-fast-forward rejection:

```js
return text.indexOf('non-fast-forward') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('[rejected]') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('fetch first') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('behind') !== -1;
```

`behind` is a common English word — an unrelated failure whose message happens to contain it (a pre-receive hook message, a proxy/infra error mentioning "behind", a path segment) would be misclassified as healable. The harm is bounded (one fetch + merge + retry, then the honest error surfaces), but the misclassification also muddies the failure class in logs and wastes a merge attempt in the agent's working tree mid-run.

Suggest anchoring to the actual git hint shape — `" is behind"` or `"tip of your current branch is behind"` — which the suite's own test names already imply ("behind-hint shape"). Note `String(err)` vs `err.message`: `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR.js:325` classifies with `String(mergeErr)` (message + stack); `error.message` alone is fine here since the CLI error carries the git output, just keep it deliberate.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the stale-zombie aging advertised in the comment is untested**

The function comment promises: *"plus the same stale-zombie window the dispatch guard applies (a leg stuck 'queued' for hours ages out)"*, implemented via:

```js
if (status !== 'in_progress' && isStaleNonRunningWorkflowRun(r, status)) return false;
```

None of the six new `gh-798` tests covers this path. A regression here is silent and asymmetrical: dropping the line would make a zombie `queued` leg (e.g. a runner-capacity stuck run) freeze branch freshness for `STALE_NON_RUNNING_WORKFLOW_MS` = 6h, and nothing would fail.

    // legRun('queued') + updated_at older than STALE_NON_RUNNING_WORKFLOW_MS

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the `uHead`-null fallback still pushes under an unproven head — document the residual-race contract**

When the head sha cannot be resolved (`resolveHeadSha` → `null` on a transient API failure), the refresh proceeds with **no in-flight-leg probe at all** — exactly the incident shape this PR fixes can still occur through this hole:

```js
} else {
    // No resolvable head sha: no probe possible — the
    // pre-gh-798 behavior stands (refresh rides the branch
    // name alone).
    silentUpdateBranch(ticket.branch);
```

Fail-open here is a defensible, deliberate choice (consistent with `resolveHeadSha`'s own contract, and the timer-side `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` is the backstop), but the comment should say so explicitly — i.e. that a leg racing an unprobed refresh is healed harness-side rather than prevented. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-798` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +466
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T19:52:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T20:17:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #798
### Root Cause
`sm-silent-update` (`silent-update-behind` → `update_branch` in `js/smAgent.js`) refreshed every BEHIND PR unconditionally — its only in-flight exclusion was `ai_validating`, so a rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` leg running on the PR head (dispatched with `workflowRef={branch}`) had `main` merged under it mid-run, and the leg's timer WIP auto-save (`js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`, bare `git push origin HEAD`) was rejected non-fast-forward (live: fa PR #1420, run 37828431528). The timer had no non-FF self-heal, so the raw failure surfaced to the running agent.

### Fix
- `js/smAgent.js` — `update_branch` now probes the head sha for active (queued/in_progress/waiting/pending) ai-teammate runs before refreshing (new `hasActiveLegRun`, the `hasActiveHeadRun` pattern narrowed to the leg workflow; probe fresh every tick; probe failure fails closed). The refresh is not lost — the BEHIND PR refreshes on the first tick after the leg finishes.
- `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js` — new `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` wrapper: on a non-FF rejection the timer fetches + merges the branch (merge-style, matching the SM's own refreshes) and retries the push once; a conflicted heal merge is aborted, and any other failure surfaces honestly.

### Test Coverage
- `test_smAgent.js`: 6 new gh-798 tests — running + queued leg defer the refresh, finished leg restores it (per-tick freshness), unrelated CI never blocks, probe failure fails closed, no-leg path is command-identical.
- `test_timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`: new wrapper suite — mock remote rejecting once → fetch/merge/retry lands; retry failure, merge conflict (abort), non-FF-only gating, end-to-end tick.
- Full `run_all.json`: **1926 passed, 0 failed** (validation-leg exclusion unchanged).

### Notes
- The exclusion keys on the dispatch-run probe only (per the ticket's recommendation) — labels are set/cleared by the legs and can be stale.
- `pushReworkChanges.js` already self-heals its push (fetch+merge+retry); unchanged.
- One existing test was tightened: the gh-750 probe-count test now counts only the dispatched-verdict probe shape (the new gh-798 leg probe is a separate all-workflows rollup call).

# gh-798: [BUG] sm-silent-update pushes under an in-flight rework leg — timer auto-save push fails non-fast-forward mid-run (live: fa PR #1420, run 37828431528)

## Description

## Goal — Silent-update vs in-flight rework: the race that breaks the agent's timer pushes (v1)

One sentence: **a rework leg never again fights the SM's own silent branch refresh — `silent-update-behind` gains an in-flight-rework exclusion, and the harness-side timer push learns to survive a legitimate mid-run base refresh.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415 rework leg, run 37828431528, 2026-10-08):
- 19:13 — harness timer WIP auto-save pushed fine.
- 19:15:20 — `sm-silent-update` merged main into `ai/gh-1415` and pushed `f76db206` **while the rework leg was running on that branch**.
- 19:18 — second timer auto-save committed locally on the now-stale branch.
- 19:23 — timer push `git push origin HEAD` → **rejected (non-fast-forward), exit 1** — "⏱️ timer: git push failed" surfaced to the agent mid-run.
- 19:28 — the agent manually recovered (merged origin, pushed the real fix `d11a5670`, closed 4/4 review threads).

The leg survived by improvisation. The race is real: `silent-update-behind` excludes `ai_validating` ("so the validation head never moves mid-run") but has **no exclusion for an in-flight rework/review leg**, whose session is anchored to the exact branch state it checked out.

## Why this framing

- The rework leg's post-action, prompts, and thread-preparation (`preCliReworkSetup.js` → `pr_discussions.md`) all behaved correctly on this incident — the break was the mid-run base move, not the input pipeline.
- `ai_validating` exclusion already establishes the precedent: heads with a leg in flight must not move. This card extends the same invariant to rework/review legs.

## Architecture

1. **SM side (`js/smAgent.js` silent-update-behind / the shared `update_branch` path):** exclude PRs with an in-flight rework or review leg from silent refresh — the same detection the rerun/other rules already use (the `hasActiveHeadRun` pattern: any dispatched rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` run on the head in `queued`/`in_progress`, or the `agent:rework` label while a leg runs). The refresh is not lost — the PR is BEHIND and refreshes on the first tick after the leg finishes.
2. **Harness-side hardening (`pushReworkChanges.js` post-action and/or the timer push wrapper — whichever owns the bare `git push origin HEAD`):** a non-fast-forward rejection must self-heal — `git pull --no-rebase` (merge, matching the SM's own merge-style refreshes) then retry the push, once, before surfacing the failure. The agent's manual recovery (merge origin → push) is exactly this; encode it.
3. Ordering invariant: the exclusion must be checked at tick time (fresh state), not cached — an in-flight leg starts/stops between ticks.

## Capability surface

| path | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| rework/review leg in flight + PR BEHIND | silent-update pushes under the leg → timer push non-FF fails mid-run | leg excluded from refresh until it finishes; refresh happens on the next tick |
| timer push hits non-FF anyway (any residual race) | raw failure surfaced to the agent | one auto pull-merge + retry, then honest failure |
| validation legs | excluded (ai_validating) | unchanged |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — silent-update skips a BEHIND PR whose head has an in-flight (queued or running) rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` dispatch; refresh happens on the tick after the leg completes.
- **AC2** — the exclusion is evaluated per tick (a leg that finished between ticks does not block the refresh).
- **AC3** — a non-FF timer/post-action push self-heals via one pull-merge + retry and lands the commit (unit-tested push wrapper with a mock remote that rejects once).
- **AC4** — validation exclusion behavior unchanged (existing tests green).

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — silent-update query/action tests: mocked PR with in-flight dispatch (queued and running variants) → no push command emitted; leg finished → push emitted.
- `UT-*` — push-wrapper test: first push rejected non-FF → pull-merge → retry succeeds (AC3).
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green on the dmtools runtime; existing silent-update tests stay green (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Changing the validation-leg exclusion semantics.
- Making silent-update rebase instead of merge (the SM's merge-style refresh is load-bearing elsewhere).
- Harness-repo changes (the push wrapper lives in the rework job's JS / factory scripts, both in this repo's orbit).

## Open questions

- Whether the exclusion keys on the dispatch-run probe alone or also on the `agent:rework`/`agent:review` labels (recommend: the run probe — labels are set/cleared by the legs themselves and can be stale).

## References

- Live timeline: run 37828431528 (16:07 leg → 19:13/19:18 WIP saves, 19:15 silent-update `f76db206`, 19:23 push failure, 19:28 agent self-recovery `d11a5670`, 4/4 threads resolved).
- `silent-update-behind` rule (ai_validating exclusion rationale, limit 20); `preCliReworkSetup.js` (input prep, correct); `pushReworkChanges.js` (post-action push owner).

- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37835258454) · started 19:53 · done 20:05 ✅

### Thread 1 — `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `docs-freshness` CI is red — regenerated agent docs not committed (reproduced locally)**

The `docs-freshness` check failed on commit `7f9c1e57` ([run 37835253514](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37835253514/job/113510522008)). Root cause confirmed locally: the new `git merge` command in `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` changes the side-effect list the doc generator extracts from `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`, and the committed generated docs are stale. Running `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` on this branch produces:

```diff
--- docs/agents/generated/bug_development.md
+++ docs/agents/generated/bug_development.md
   - Side effects:
     - git push
+    - git merge
```

The same stale diff applies to `docs/agents/generated/pr_rework.md` and `docs/agents/generated/story_development.md` (all three embed the timer module).

**Fix** (mechanical):

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git add docs/agents/generated
git commit -m "docs: regenerate agent docs — timer gains a git merge side effect (gh-798)"
```

The code fix itself is sound — this is only the missing docs regeneration, but it is a red merge gate and must land before merge.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the bare `'behind'` substring is a loose non-FF signal**

`isNonFastForwardError` treats *any* error text containing `behind` as a healable non-fast-forward rejection:

```js
return text.indexOf('non-fast-forward') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('[rejected]') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('fetch first') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('behind') !== -1;
```

`behind` is a common English word — an unrelated failure whose message happens to contain it (a pre-receive hook message, a proxy/infra error mentioning "behind", a path segment) would be misclassified as healable. The harm is bounded (one fetch + merge + retry, then the honest error surfaces), but the misclassification also muddies the failure class in logs and wastes a merge attempt in the agent's working tree mid-run.

Suggest anchoring to the actual git hint shape — `" is behind"` or `"tip of your current branch is behind"` — which the suite's own test names already imply ("behind-hint shape"). Note `String(err)` vs `err.message`: `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR.js:325` classifies with `String(mergeErr)` (message + stack); `error.message` alone is fine here since the CLI error carries the git output, just keep it deliberate.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the stale-zombie aging advertised in the comment is untested**

The function comment promises: *"plus the same stale-zombie window the dispatch guard applies (a leg stuck 'queued' for hours ages out)"*, implemented via:

```js
if (status !== 'in_progress' && isStaleNonRunningWorkflowRun(r, status)) return false;
```

None of the six new `gh-798` tests covers this path. A regression here is silent and asymmetrical: dropping the line would make a zombie `queued` leg (e.g. a runner-capacity stuck run) freeze branch freshness for `STALE_NON_RUNNING_WORKFLOW_MS` = 6h, and nothing would fail.

Cheap addition alongside the QUEUED variant test:

```js
test('gh-798: a STALE queued leg (zombie) ages out and does not block', function () {
    // legRun('queued') + updated_at older than STALE_NON_RUNNING_WORKFLOW_MS
    // → updateCommands(sm).length === 1
});
```

(The other five behaviors — running, queued, finished, unrelated-CI, probe-failure, no-leg identity — are well covered.)

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the `uHead`-null fallback still pushes under an unproven head — document the residual-race contract**

When the head sha cannot be resolved (`resolveHeadSha` → `null` on a transient API failure), the refresh proceeds with **no in-flight-leg probe at all** — exactly the incident shape this PR fixes can still occur through this hole:

```js
} else {
    // No resolvable head sha: no probe possible — the
    // pre-gh-798 behavior stands (refresh rides the branch
    // name alone).
    silentUpdateBranch(ticket.branch);
```

Fail-open here is a defensible, deliberate choice (consistent with `resolveHeadSha`'s own contract, and the timer-side `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` is the backstop), but the comment should say so explicitly — i.e. that a leg racing an unprobed refresh is healed harness-side rather than prevented. Alternatively, failing closed (defer the refresh when the head is known to exist but unresolvable) costs one tick and closes the hole completely. Either way, one sentence in the comment makes the residual-risk contract greppable for the next incident bisect.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: third copy of the fetch+merge+retry heal — consider a shared canonical helper**

The non-FF self-heal now exists in three shapes:

- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (inline `fetch → merge → push` retry, lines ~325-333)
- `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` (this PR — adds FF gating, conflict abort, branch resolution)
- `syncBranchWithBase` (`js/common/pullRequest.js` — the merge-style sync used pre-push)

This repo has already canonicalized exactly this class of drifting git probes (`mergeState.js` header: *"Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe … same canonical-helper rationale as gitStaging.js — duplicated probes drift"*). A future fix to one copy (e.g. the `'behind'` matcher, submodule fetch flag, conflict-abort behavior) will not reach the others.

Not requesting a refactor in this bugfix PR — keeping `pushReworkChanges.js` untouched is the right scope call — but a follow-up to move `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` (or its core) into `js/common/` and have `pushReworkChanges.js` delegate would leave one heal to maintain.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json

- **Title**: gh-798 [BUG] sm-silent-update pushes under an in-flight rework leg — timer auto-save push fails non-fast-forward mid-run (live: fa PR #1420, run 37828431528)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-798` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +466
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T19:52:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T20:17:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #798
### Root Cause
`sm-silent-update` (`silent-update-behind` → `update_branch` in `js/smAgent.js`) refreshed every BEHIND PR unconditionally — its only in-flight exclusion was `ai_validating`, so a rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` leg running on the PR head (dispatched with `workflowRef={branch}`) had `main` merged under it mid-run, and the leg's timer WIP auto-save (`js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`, bare `git push origin HEAD`) was rejected non-fast-forward (live: fa PR #1420, run 37828431528). The timer had no non-FF self-heal, so the raw failure surfaced to the running agent.

### Fix
- `js/smAgent.js` — `update_branch` now probes the head sha for active (queued/in_progress/waiting/pending) ai-teammate runs before refreshing (new `hasActiveLegRun`, the `hasActiveHeadRun` pattern narrowed to the leg workflow; probe fresh every tick; probe failure fails closed). The refresh is not lost — the BEHIND PR refreshes on the first tick after the leg finishes.
- `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js` — new `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` wrapper: on a non-FF rejection the timer fetches + merges the branch (merge-style, matching the SM's own refreshes) and retries the push once; a conflicted heal merge is aborted, and any other failure surfaces honestly.

### Test Coverage
- `test_smAgent.js`: 6 new gh-798 tests — running + queued leg defer the refresh, finished leg restores it (per-tick freshness), unrelated CI never blocks, probe failure fails closed, no-leg path is command-identical.
- `test_timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`: new wrapper suite — mock remote rejecting once → fetch/merge/retry lands; retry failure, merge conflict (abort), non-FF-only gating, end-to-end tick.
- Full `run_all.json`: **1926 passed, 0 failed** (validation-leg exclusion unchanged).

### Notes
- The exclusion keys on the dispatch-run probe only (per the ticket's recommendation) — labels are set/cleared by the legs and can be stale.
- `pushReworkChanges.js` already self-heals its push (fetch+merge+retry); unchanged.
- One existing test was tightened: the gh-750 probe-count test now counts only the dispatched-verdict probe shape (the new gh-798 leg probe is a separate all-workflows rollup call).

# gh-798: [BUG] sm-silent-update pushes under an in-flight rework leg — timer auto-save push fails non-fast-forward mid-run (live: fa PR #1420, run 37828431528)

## Description

## Goal — Silent-update vs in-flight rework: the race that breaks the agent's timer pushes (v1)

One sentence: **a rework leg never again fights the SM's own silent branch refresh — `silent-update-behind` gains an in-flight-rework exclusion, and the harness-side timer push learns to survive a legitimate mid-run base refresh.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415 rework leg, run 37828431528, 2026-10-08):
- 19:13 — harness timer WIP auto-save pushed fine.
- 19:15:20 — `sm-silent-update` merged main into `ai/gh-1415` and pushed `f76db206` **while the rework leg was running on that branch**.
- 19:18 — second timer auto-save committed locally on the now-stale branch.
- 19:23 — timer push `git push origin HEAD` → **rejected (non-fast-forward), exit 1** — "⏱️ timer: git push failed" surfaced to the agent mid-run.
- 19:28 — the agent manually recovered (merged origin, pushed the real fix `d11a5670`, closed 4/4 review threads).

The leg survived by improvisation. The race is real: `silent-update-behind` excludes `ai_validating` ("so the validation head never moves mid-run") but has **no exclusion for an in-flight rework/review leg**, whose session is anchored to the exact branch state it checked out.

## Why this framing

- The rework leg's post-action, prompts, and thread-preparation (`preCliReworkSetup.js` → `pr_discussions.md`) all behaved correctly on this incident — the break was the mid-run base move, not the input pipeline.
- `ai_validating` exclusion already establishes the precedent: heads with a leg in flight must not move. This card extends the same invariant to rework/review legs.

## Architecture

1. **SM side (`js/smAgent.js` silent-update-behind / the shared `update_branch` path):** exclude PRs with an in-flight rework or review leg from silent refresh — the same detection the rerun/other rules already use (the `hasActiveHeadRun` pattern: any dispatched rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` run on the head in `queued`/`in_progress`, or the `agent:rework` label while a leg runs). The refresh is not lost — the PR is BEHIND and refreshes on the first tick after the leg finishes.
2. **Harness-side hardening (`pushReworkChanges.js` post-action and/or the timer push wrapper — whichever owns the bare `git push origin HEAD`):** a non-fast-forward rejection must self-heal — `git pull --no-rebase` (merge, matching the SM's own merge-style refreshes) then retry the push, once, before surfacing the failure. The agent's manual recovery (merge origin → push) is exactly this; encode it.
3. Ordering invariant: the exclusion must be checked at tick time (fresh state), not cached — an in-flight leg starts/stops between ticks.

## Capability surface

| path | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| rework/review leg in flight + PR BEHIND | silent-update pushes under the leg → timer push non-FF fails mid-run | leg excluded from refresh until it finishes; refresh happens on the next tick |
| timer push hits non-FF anyway (any residual race) | raw failure surfaced to the agent | one auto pull-merge + retry, then honest failure |
| validation legs | excluded (ai_validating) | unchanged |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — silent-update skips a BEHIND PR whose head has an in-flight (queued or running) rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` dispatch; refresh happens on the tick after the leg completes.
- **AC2** — the exclusion is evaluated per tick (a leg that finished between ticks does not block the refresh).
- **AC3** — a non-FF timer/post-action push self-heals via one pull-merge + retry and lands the commit (unit-tested push wrapper with a mock remote that rejects once).
- **AC4** — validation exclusion behavior unchanged (existing tests green).

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — silent-update query/action tests: mocked PR with in-flight dispatch (queued and running variants) → no push command emitted; leg finished → push emitted.
- `UT-*` — push-wrapper test: first push rejected non-FF → pull-merge → retry succeeds (AC3).
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green on the dmtools runtime; existing silent-update tests stay green (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Changing the validation-leg exclusion semantics.
- Making silent-update rebase instead of merge (the SM's merge-style refresh is load-bearing elsewhere).
- Harness-repo changes (the push wrapper lives in the rework job's JS / factory scripts, both in this repo's orbit).

## Open questions

- Whether the exclusion keys on the dispatch-run probe alone or also on the `agent:rework`/`agent:review` labels (recommend: the run probe — labels are set/cleared by the legs themselves and can be stale).

## References

- Live timeline: run 37828431528 (16:07 leg → 19:13/19:18 WIP saves, 19:15 silent-update `f76db206`, 19:23 push failure, 19:28 agent self-recovery `d11a5670`, 4/4 threads resolved).
- `silent-update-behind` rule (ai_validating exclusion rationale, limit 20); `preCliReworkSetup.js` (input prep, correct); `pushReworkChanges.js` (post-action push owner).

- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37835258454) · started 19:53 · done 20:05 ✅

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #800._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `docs-freshness` CI is red — regenerated agent docs not committed (reproduced locally)**

The `docs-freshness` check failed on commit `7f9c1e57` ([run 37835253514](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37835253514/job/113510522008)). Root cause confirmed locally: the new `git merge` command in `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` changes the side-effect list the doc generator extracts from `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`, and the committed generated docs are stale. Running `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` on this branch produces:

```diff
--- docs/agents/generated/bug_development.md
+++ docs/agents/generated/bug_development.md
   - Side effects:
     - git push
+    - git merge
```

The same stale diff applies to `docs/agents/generated/pr_rework.md` and `docs/agents/generated/story_development.md` (all three embed the timer module).

**Fix** (mechanical):

```bash
node js/agentDocGenerator.js
git add docs/agents/generated
git commit -m "docs: regenerate agent docs — timer gains a git merge side effect (gh-798)"
```

The code fix itself is sound — this is only the missing docs regeneration, but it is a red merge gate and must land before merge.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the bare `'behind'` substring is a loose non-FF signal**

`isNonFastForwardError` treats *any* error text containing `behind` as a healable non-fast-forward rejection:

```js
return text.indexOf('non-fast-forward') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('[rejected]') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('fetch first') !== -1 ||
    text.indexOf('behind') !== -1;
```

`behind` is a common English word — an unrelated failure whose message happens to contain it (a pre-receive hook message, a proxy/infra error mentioning "behind", a path segment) would be misclassified as healable. The harm is bounded (one fetch + merge + retry, then the honest error surfaces), but the misclassification also muddies the failure class in logs and wastes a merge attempt in the agent's working tree mid-run.

Suggest anchoring to the actual git hint shape — `" is behind"` or `"tip of your current branch is behind"` — which the suite's own test names already imply ("behind-hint shape"). Note `String(err)` vs `err.message`: `mergeStoryTestAutomationPR.js:325` classifies with `String(mergeErr)` (message + stack); `error.message` alone is fine here since the CLI error carries the git output, just keep it deliberate.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the stale-zombie aging advertised in the comment is untested**

The function comment promises: *"plus the same stale-zombie window the dispatch guard applies (a leg stuck 'queued' for hours ages out)"*, implemented via:

```js
if (status !== 'in_progress' && isStaleNonRunningWorkflowRun(r, status)) return false;
```

None of the six new `gh-798` tests covers this path. A regression here is silent and asymmetrical: dropping the line would make a zombie `queued` leg (e.g. a runner-capacity stuck run) freeze branch freshness for `STALE_NON_RUNNING_WORKFLOW_MS` = 6h, and nothing would fail.

Cheap addition alongside the QUEUED variant test:

```js
test('gh-798: a STALE queued leg (zombie) ages out and does not block', function () {
    // legRun('queued') + updated_at older than STALE_NON_RUNNING_WORKFLOW_MS
    // → updateCommands(sm).length === 1
});
```

(The other five behaviors — running, queued, finished, unrelated-CI, probe-failure, no-leg identity — are well covered.)

---

### Thread 4 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the `uHead`-null fallback still pushes under an unproven head — document the residual-race contract**

When the head sha cannot be resolved (`resolveHeadSha` → `null` on a transient API failure), the refresh proceeds with **no in-flight-leg probe at all** — exactly the incident shape this PR fixes can still occur through this hole:

```js
} else {
    // No resolvable head sha: no probe possible — the
    // pre-gh-798 behavior stands (refresh rides the branch
    // name alone).
    silentUpdateBranch(ticket.branch);
```

Fail-open here is a defensible, deliberate choice (consistent with `resolveHeadSha`'s own contract, and the timer-side `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` is the backstop), but the comment should say so explicitly — i.e. that a leg racing an unprobed refresh is healed harness-side rather than prevented. Alternatively, failing closed (defer the refresh when the head is known to exist but unresolvable) costs one tick and closes the hole completely. Either way, one sentence in the comment makes the residual-risk contract greppable for the next incident bisect.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
💡 **SUGGESTION: third copy of the fetch+merge+retry heal — consider a shared canonical helper**

The non-FF self-heal now exists in three shapes:

- `js/pushReworkChanges.js` (inline `fetch → merge → push` retry, lines ~325-333)
- `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` (this PR — adds FF gating, conflict abort, branch resolution)
- `syncBranchWithBase` (`js/common/pullRequest.js` — the merge-style sync used pre-push)

This repo has already canonicalized exactly this class of drifting git probes (`mergeState.js` header: *"Every commit- or merge-producing site must consult this ONE probe … same canonical-helper rationale as gitStaging.js — duplicated probes drift"*). A future fix to one copy (e.g. the `'behind'` matcher, submodule fetch flag, conflict-abort behavior) will not reach the others.

Not requesting a refactor in this bugfix PR — keeping `pushReworkChanges.js` untouched is the right scope call — but a follow-up to move `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` (or its core) into `js/common/` and have `pushReworkChanges.js` delegate would leave one heal to maintain.

---

### Thread 6

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-08):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-798 fix itself is sound — the SM-side in-flight-leg exclusion (`hasActiveLegRun`, fresh probe per tick, fail-closed) and the timer's one-shot non-FF self-heal match the ticket's architecture and all four ACs; both affected suites pass locally (smAgent 355 ✅, timer 27 ✅). One BLOCKING gate: `docs-freshness` CI is red — the new `git merge` side effect in `timerAutoCommitAndSave.js` was never propagated into `docs/agents/generated/` (stale: `bug_development.md`, `pr_rework.md`, `story_development.md`; reproduced locally via `node js/agentDocGenerator.js`).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json
Now let me verify the docs staleness locally by running the generator and checking the diff. First, let me confirm node is available.

## PR Description

Closes #798
### Root Cause
`sm-silent-update` (`silent-update-behind` → `update_branch` in `js/smAgent.js`) refreshed every BEHIND PR unconditionally — its only in-flight exclusion was `ai_validating`, so a rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` leg running on the PR head (dispatched with `workflowRef={branch}`) had `main` merged under it mid-run, and the leg's timer WIP auto-save (`js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`, bare `git push origin HEAD`) was rejected non-fast-forward (live: fa PR #1420, run 37828431528). The timer had no non-FF self-heal, so the raw failure surfaced to the running agent.

### Fix
- `js/smAgent.js` — `update_branch` now probes the head sha for active (queued/in_progress/waiting/pending) ai-teammate runs before refreshing (new `hasActiveLegRun`, the `hasActiveHeadRun` pattern narrowed to the leg workflow; probe fresh every tick; probe failure fails closed). The refresh is not lost — the BEHIND PR refreshes on the first tick after the leg finishes.
- `js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js` — new `pushBranchWithSelfHeal` wrapper: on a non-FF rejection the timer fetches + merges the branch (merge-style, matching the SM's own refreshes) and retries the push once; a conflicted heal merge is aborted, and any other failure surfaces honestly.

### Test Coverage
- `test_smAgent.js`: 6 new gh-798 tests — running + queued leg defer the refresh, finished leg restores it (per-tick freshness), unrelated CI never blocks, probe failure fails closed, no-leg path is command-identical.
- `test_timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`: new wrapper suite — mock remote rejecting once → fetch/merge/retry lands; retry failure, merge conflict (abort), non-FF-only gating, end-to-end tick.
- Full `run_all.json`: **1926 passed, 0 failed** (validation-leg exclusion unchanged).

### Notes
- The exclusion keys on the dispatch-run probe only (per the ticket's recommendation) — labels are set/cleared by the legs and can be stale.
- `pushReworkChanges.js` already self-heals its push (fetch+merge+retry); unchanged.
- One existing test was tightened: the gh-750 probe-count test now counts only the dispatched-verdict probe shape (the new gh-798 leg probe is a separate all-workflows rollup call).

# gh-798: [BUG] sm-silent-update pushes under an in-flight rework leg — timer auto-save push fails non-fast-forward mid-run (live: fa PR #1420, run 37828431528)

## Description

## Goal — Silent-update vs in-flight rework: the race that breaks the agent's timer pushes (v1)

One sentence: **a rework leg never again fights the SM's own silent branch refresh — `silent-update-behind` gains an in-flight-rework exclusion, and the harness-side timer push learns to survive a legitimate mid-run base refresh.**

Live evidence (fa PR #1420 / gh-1415 rework leg, run 37828431528, 2026-10-08):
- 19:13 — harness timer WIP auto-save pushed fine.
- 19:15:20 — `sm-silent-update` merged main into `ai/gh-1415` and pushed `f76db206` **while the rework leg was running on that branch**.
- 19:18 — second timer auto-save committed locally on the now-stale branch.
- 19:23 — timer push `git push origin HEAD` → **rejected (non-fast-forward), exit 1** — "⏱️ timer: git push failed" surfaced to the agent mid-run.
- 19:28 — the agent manually recovered (merged origin, pushed the real fix `d11a5670`, closed 4/4 review threads).

The leg survived by improvisation. The race is real: `silent-update-behind` excludes `ai_validating` ("so the validation head never moves mid-run") but has **no exclusion for an in-flight rework/review leg**, whose session is anchored to the exact branch state it checked out.

## Why this framing

- The rework leg's post-action, prompts, and thread-preparation (`preCliReworkSetup.js` → `pr_discussions.md`) all behaved correctly on this incident — the break was the mid-run base move, not the input pipeline.
- `ai_validating` exclusion already establishes the precedent: heads with a leg in flight must not move. This card extends the same invariant to rework/review legs.

## Architecture

1. **SM side (`js/smAgent.js` silent-update-behind / the shared `update_branch` path):** exclude PRs with an in-flight rework or review leg from silent refresh — the same detection the rerun/other rules already use (the `hasActiveHeadRun` pattern: any dispatched rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` run on the head in `queued`/`in_progress`, or the `agent:rework` label while a leg runs). The refresh is not lost — the PR is BEHIND and refreshes on the first tick after the leg finishes.
2. **Harness-side hardening (`pushReworkChanges.js` post-action and/or the timer push wrapper — whichever owns the bare `git push origin HEAD`):** a non-fast-forward rejection must self-heal — `git pull --no-rebase` (merge, matching the SM's own merge-style refreshes) then retry the push, once, before surfacing the failure. The agent's manual recovery (merge origin → push) is exactly this; encode it.
3. Ordering invariant: the exclusion must be checked at tick time (fresh state), not cached — an in-flight leg starts/stops between ticks.

## Capability surface

| path | today | after |
|---|---|---|
| rework/review leg in flight + PR BEHIND | silent-update pushes under the leg → timer push non-FF fails mid-run | leg excluded from refresh until it finishes; refresh happens on the next tick |
| timer push hits non-FF anyway (any residual race) | raw failure surfaced to the agent | one auto pull-merge + retry, then honest failure |
| validation legs | excluded (ai_validating) | unchanged |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — silent-update skips a BEHIND PR whose head has an in-flight (queued or running) rework/review `ai-teammate.yml` dispatch; refresh happens on the tick after the leg completes.
- **AC2** — the exclusion is evaluated per tick (a leg that finished between ticks does not block the refresh).
- **AC3** — a non-FF timer/post-action push self-heals via one pull-merge + retry and lands the commit (unit-tested push wrapper with a mock remote that rejects once).
- **AC4** — validation exclusion behavior unchanged (existing tests green).

## Test plan

- `UT-*` — silent-update query/action tests: mocked PR with in-flight dispatch (queued and running variants) → no push command emitted; leg finished → push emitted.
- `UT-*` — push-wrapper test: first push rejected non-FF → pull-merge → retry succeeds (AC3).
- `REG` — full `run_all.json` green on the dmtools runtime; existing silent-update tests stay green (AC4).

## Non-goals

- Changing the validation-leg exclusion semantics.
- Making silent-update rebase instead of merge (the SM's merge-style refresh is load-bearing elsewhere).
- Harness-repo changes (the push wrapper lives in the rework job's JS / factory scripts, both in this repo's orbit).

## Open questions

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems
